target_customer: Asset managers and general partners (private equity, credit, hedge funds) whose investor relations and compliance teams answer due diligence questionnaires and RFPs
problem: Fundraising teams spend days filling due diligence questionnaires with recycled content for each prospective investor.
product_category: AI for institutional fundraising, DDQ and RFP automation

founders.name: Mamal Amini
founders.background_notes: Machine learning scientist who reports co-authoring models with Yoshua Bengio and Doina Precup, per the YC page. Employers not clearly named.

founders.name: Oliver Walerys
founders.background_notes: Self-taught product and software builder and a longtime friend of Mamal Amini.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval and drafting over a firm's approved answer library, with approval tracking and security audits, is standard LLM application work. Accuracy and trust needs in finance add difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Generic RFP tools can add AI. Customers' answer libraries and workflow integrations create some lock in once loaded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established RFP software vendors exist and CB Insights lists them as top competitors. No acquisition of GovernGPT was found.

market_need_then: The YC pitch said teams dedicate days to questionnaires. At the time of the batch the company was piloting with a private credit firm, a hedge fund and a private equity firm, per the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as the Institutional-Fundraising Brain and a category of one

brand_strength.rationale: A GPT suffix name that ties to the 2023 generative AI wave but sounds like a government product, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: GovernGPT is active, sells to named institutions such as Pantheon, Coatue and Stonepeak by its own listing, and publishes SOC 2 and customer claims. No confirmed funding beyond Y Combinator was found, with aggregators showing a 500K convertible note unverified. The sales pace seems real, but the lack of public funding makes it hard to judge scale against Loopio and Responsive.
notes: CB Insights and VCBacked list a 500K convertible note dated 2024-01-01 (aggregators, single source, not recorded as a round). The YC page said a seed was planned. Locations conflict between Montreal and Toronto. Competitor sources found are 2026 vendor blogs and CB Insights without dates near the batch, so the list is empty. Education and employers not stated on the YC page beyond McKinsey being named for the founders collectively. Completeness pass: Round rests on aggregators (CB Insights convertible note Jan 2024, VCBacked pre-seed Apr 2024); month conflicts so only the year is recorded.
